subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source, docs, and tests encode persistent session defaults, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Make config the upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields that exceed current global or agent policy, with migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

options.title: Keep persistent session overrides
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Add operator reset first
options.body: Ship an explicit session exec reset or doctor repair path before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make config the upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields that exceed current global or agent policy, with migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the `/exec` session override feature and the exec defaults resolver points to this owner path.
